lines.content: dependency on a published object explicit, and lets a page ship without a map.
**The bulk deletion is quarantined.** Removing the inline SVGs from 94 pages is unavoidable once the
pages reference assets, but it is mechanical. It lands as its own commit (and can be its own PR)
touching only `docs/problems/*.md`, so the code review is the small diff.
pages reference assets — 19.6 MB of committed markup cannot leave the tree without a large deletion
diff — but it is mechanical and self-verifying. It lands as its own commit touching only
`docs/problems/*.md`, so the code review is the small diff, and the deletion commit is checked by
assertion rather than by reading: every hunk is a removed `<circle>`/`<rect>` run,
`grep -c '<svg' docs/problems/*.md` is 0 afterwards, and the directory drops from 19.6 MB to under
200 KB. It can be merged on its own, ahead of or behind the code.
- [ ] `docs/problems/` shrinks from 19.6 MB to under 200 KB, and the code diff (excluding the
quarantined deletion commit) is under ~600 lines.
- [ ] The deletion commit is verifiable without reading it: it touches only `docs/problems/*.md`,
no `<svg` remains, and the frontmatter gained exactly the minimap fields.

changes.title: feat(web): serve problem minimaps from R2 instead of inlining them in the docs

commit.message:
task(web): say how the bulk deletion commit is reviewed

Removing 19.6 MB of inline SVG cannot be a small diff, so the criterion is that
the deletion commit is verified by assertion — only docs/problems/*.md touched,
no <svg left, frontmatter gained exactly the minimap fields — rather than by
reading 223k removed lines.
